title: A Wild Sprint Stantler Hops a Route 29 NPC from rest

verification.actor: One prepared current Wild Stantler (species 234) idle at map 33 tile (599,395), with the resolved Sprint lane and attached presentation
verification.trigger: At the common Wild direction-choice entry, choose East for one obstacle request from (599,395); leave stock collision and motion code unchanged
verification.observable: One two-tile Hop crosses the stock Route 29 NPC tile (600,395), lands at (601,395), and returns control. Native terrain reports all three tiles loaded and statically open.

setupMutations.change: Use a disposable save, checked map 33 teleport to player (604,395), native Wild Stantler spawn at (599,395), and exact-subject bind. Do not modify the stock NPC.
The bounded native control changes only r1 to East at one Wild direction-choice call from (599,395). It does not write game memory, force a return value, change the Sprint lane or admit a motion.

limits: The stock Route 29 event places an NPC at (600,395). The runtime receipt proves a statically open midpoint and the native Hop decision, but does not directly read the NPC object identity. The NPC occupancy is inferred from fixed map event data.

This controlled direction choice proves the shared Wild caller and Sprint movement policy for one NPC obstacle. It does not prove a planned Walk-to-Hop route, natural Wander RNG, Chase targeting, Flee targeting or natural population spawning.
Copied-data controls reject false terrain, changed actor, altered direction register, wrong start, short Hop and missing Hop commit. Registration alone is not accepted runtime proof.

events.value: Place the player near the stock NPC, spawn and bind Wild Sprint Stantler idle at (599,395)
Arm the bounded East direction control at the shared Wild step entry
Observe one two-tile Hop and its terminal commit under neutral input
Close the control after the two-tile landing

stop.condition: The same Stantler commits one two-tile Hop at (601,395)

invariants: Only the candidate direction register is changed; the game still accepts or rejects each motion
The takeoff, NPC midpoint and two-tile landing have loaded, statically open terrain
The Hop commits exactly once on the same current actor
The trace and completed game frames remain contiguous without a canceled motion
